problem_statement: When OpenThread fragments an IPv6 datagram that is destined to be looped back to the host, each resulting fragment ignores the loopback-to-host setting of the original datagram and is always allowed to be delivered to the host. As a result, a large datagram explicitly marked as not allowed to be looped back to the host is still delivered fragment-by-fragment to the host receive callback, and OpenThread-generated ICMPv6 messages (errors and echo replies) and ping echo requests are not consistently delivered to the host. The behavior required is that a fragmented datagram inherits the loopback-to-host flag of the original datagram (so fragments of a not-allowed datagram are not passed to the host), and that OpenThread-generated ICMPv6 messages and ping echo requests are passed to the host.
oracle_note: observed by validate_instance.py (fail before, pass after the fix); the unit oracle is per executable, so check attribution of the cases to the PR's change
